column1: # q27 model registry — drives `q27 pull`, `q27 bench`, `q27 serve`.
# One line per installable pack. TAB-separated. # lines are comments.
# The wrapper reads this file (installed next to it by the formula).
# Columns (TAB-separated, no leading/trailing spaces):
#   1 name          short handle the user types (`q27 pull <name>`)
#   2 display       human label
#   3 quant_policy  artifact's quant_policy metadata value (route selector)
#   4 artifact_file the .q27 filename inside the model dir
#   5 artifact_md5  expected md5 of the artifact (empty if unverified/unknown)
#   6 weights_gb    artifact size in GiB (bytes/2^30), for fit checks
#   7 min_ram_gb    practical minimum unified memory (GiB) to run + starter ctx
#   8 hf_repo       Hugging Face repo hosting the artifact/source
#   9 source_kind   direct = download .q27 (md5-checked);
#                   repack = download GGUF, repack locally (sha256-checked);
#                   local  = produced on this machine, not downloadable
#  10 tokenizer     direct = download the .tok; gguf = export from source GGUF
#  11 experimental  yes = opt-in research pack; no = supported
#  12 notes         one-line guidance shown by `q27 pull <name>`
# Official Qwen3.6-27B-MTP tiers live in signalnine/Qwen3.6-27B-MTP-q27 and
# are direct .q27 downloads verified against that repo's CHECKSUMS.md5.
# Bonsai ternary/binary tiers are lossless repacks of prism-ml GGUFs. They are
# pre-repacked once and hosted at manthedan/q27-bonsai-packs as direct .q27
# (+ .tok) downloads verified by md5, so testers need no Python/numpy/gguf.
# The repack is deterministic and reproducible from the prism-ml GGUF via
# tools/repack.py (pinned source + artifact sha256 in q27-fetch); the hosted
# artifacts are byte-identical to that repack. q27 never redistributes the
# official checkpoint weights.
